author: Matthew Green
excerpt: Introducing velociraptor-skills, a set of reusable AI skills for DFIR with Velociraptor.
title: AI Ate My Velociraptor

author: Evgen Blohm
excerpt: In this article, we summarise our findings on a previously unknown Threat Actor targeting internal dissidents, connected to the “Rise Iran!” movement. We highlight the lures used, insights into the deployed InfoStealer we call ParsaStealer, and further insights into the Telegram channels used.
title: Iranopasmigirim - Unmasking an ever-evolving Espionage Campaign Against Iranian Dissidents - Part 1

author: Dario Weiss
excerpt: One pentest turned into 22 CVEs in TeamDavid®, a self-hosted "secure" Microsoft 365 alternative, from an unauthenticated single-request DoS to full, unauthenticated account takeover.
title: 22 CVEs in TeamDavid® a "secure" M365 alternative

author: Stephan Berger
excerpt: Analysis of a Deno-based malware intrusion that began with mailbombing and a fake Microsoft Teams IT-support call, leading a victim to execute a malicious archive. The payload is a modular JavaScript RAT/proxy framework using Deno, with components for C2 over WebSocket, local command execution…
title: Anatomy of a Deno-Based Proxy & RAT

author: Lucas Dodgson, Tobias Oberdörfer, Robin Hilber
excerpt: An analysis of a widely available Exchange Online misconfiguration allowing attackers to spoof internal and external senders.
title: Ghost-Sender - Universal Email Spoofing against Exchange Online

author: Dario Weiss, Manuel Feifel, Olivier Becker
excerpt: A widely used Secure E-Mail Gateway "SeppMail" revealed critical vulnerabilities with little effort and without chaining of multiple vulnerabilities. RCE to compromise the device, LFI to read mails and more. (CVE-2026-2743, CVE-2026-7864, CVE-2026-44127, CVE-2026-44128)
title: SeppMail Secure E-Mail Gateway: Critical RCE and LFI Vulnerabilities

author: Florian Scheiber
excerpt: This article provides an overview of BravoX, a new ransomware player whose operations combine familiar tactics with a few distinctive twists, offering insight into their techniques, tooling, and notably their negotiation approach.
title: BravoX - The new Kids on the Block

author: Evgen Blohm
excerpt: This article provides a comprehensive summary of our research into the VIPERTUNNEL Python backdoor, including infrastructure hunting and showcasing the evolution of the code.
title: Slithering Through the Noise - Deep Dive into the VIPERTUNNEL Python Backdoor

author: Manuel Feifel
excerpt: The Behavioral Indicators of Compromise (BIOCs) of Cortex XDR contain numerous exceptions, including global whitelists that can be abused to evade detection even when using simple and well-known TTPs.
title: Decrypting and Abusing Predefined BIOCs in Palo Alto Cortex XDR

author: Manuel Feifel
excerpt: The Cortex XDR agent includes an incident response feature called "Live Terminal", which attackers can abuse as a C2.
title: Abusing Cortex XDR Live Terminal as a C2

author: Matthew Green
excerpt: .NET reflection is a common technique used by threat actors throughout the attack lifecycle. In this post, I introduce two Velociraptor capabilities for hunting reflection-loaded assemblies and detecting patched or downgraded CLR instances. I also share techniques to dump suspicious assemblies for…
title: CLRaptor: Hunting reflected assemblies with Velociraptor

author: Manuel Feifel
excerpt: Attacking EDRs Part 5 - Multiple vulnerabilities are present in the communication of Defender for Endpoint with cloud APIs. Authentication bypass, spoofing of commands and data, uploading malicious data to incident responders and information disclosure.
title: Analyzing and Breaking Defender for Endpoint's Cloud Communication

author: Yann Malherbe
excerpt: Automating VHDX investigations can transform how DFIR teams handle virtual desktop environments. By integrating Velociraptor with a smart remapping workflow, this approach enables seamless analysis of virtual profiles, reducing manual effort, increasing speed, and ensuring consistent, scalable…
title: Automation of VHDX Investigations

author: Manuel Feifel
excerpt: Multiple out-of-bounds read and null dereference bugs were identified in Microsoft Defender by using Snapshot Fuzzing with WTF and kAFL/NYX. The bugs can be used to crash the main Defender process as soon as the file is scanned. Most are unpatched, but none appear exploitable for code execution.
title: Attacking EDRs Part 4: Fuzzing Defender's Scanning and Emulation Engine (mpengine.dll)

author: Manuel Feifel
excerpt: This post describes a DoS vulnerability affecting most Windows EDR agents. The vulnerability is an issue in the handling of already existing objects in the Object Manager's namespace.
title: Attacking EDRs Part 3: One Bug to Stop them all

author: Manuel Feifel
excerpt: The second part describes the process and results of the EDR driver security analysis of Palo Alto Cortex using manual analysis and Sophos Intercept X using snapshot fuzzing. Only minor vulnerabilities were identified (CVE-2024-5905).
title: Attacking EDRs Part 2: Driver Analysis Results

author: Manuel Feifel
excerpt: This article gives an overview of the attack surface of EDR software and describes the process to search for attack surface on EDR drivers from a low-privileged user.
title: Attacking EDRs Part 1: Intro & Security Analysis of EDR Drivers

author: Stephan Berger
excerpt: To gain insight into common issues and patterns of misconfiguration, we analyzed 250 PingCastle reports collected from Incident Response cases and Compromise Assessments.
title: Tear Down The Castle - Part 2

author: Stephan Berger
excerpt: To gain insight into common issues and patterns of misconfiguration, we analyzed 250 PingCastle reports collected from Incident Response cases and Compromise Assessments.
title: Tear Down The Castle - Part 1

author: Mario Bischof
excerpt: This article explains how image recognition services can be used to bypass (i.e. auto-solve) classical alphanumeric CAPTCHAs.
title: Breaking CAPTCHAs with image recognition
